result.summary:
No numerical bug found in LongHitScorer: every returned key matches an independent brute-force reference, so gp_hit_1 / rl_hit_1 are being paid what the definition says. Two design-level points (orientation rule, sh_* carrying the market's own Sharpe) are worth fixing before the next round, but neither justifies a restart.

What I covered (local only, repo untouched; scratch in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-230P-hw2/208bbacf-e83a-42e0-b6f4-3ead427e5e95/scratchpad/lh/ — ref.py is the reference, fuzz.py the driver):

- Reference comparison. Plain per-day loops written from the definition, no torch, nothing imported from alphacube. 940 randomized cases (850 with D 6-44 / S 5-69, 90 with S 100-430) plus one at S=5220, both signs, all 44 returned keys with gates off; also production defaults (gates on, both orientations, HIT_WEIGHTS/HIT_SCALES) and score_combined. Tolerance rel 1e-8.
- Inputs used to break it (each alone, then mixed): random NaN in panel and label, whole-day NaN factor (first days, middle days), whole-day NaN label (first, random, last), +-inf in panel and label, float32, days with 0..25 finite names, heavy ties, ties at top or bottom book boundary, labels exactly +-0.0, all-positive / all-negative / all-zero / constant label days, a single labelled name, unbuyable names concentrated in the book, constant-factor days, signed zeros, 1e37-scale values. 22 further degenerate inputs (all-NaN, 1-3 days, 1-5 stocks, int panel) match with no exception.
- Result: zero discrepancies in any LongHitScorer component. The only mismatches (67 of 700 cases, all with a constant-label day) are in ic / lic / long_ic and come from the pre-existing _cs_corr_days_t, not the new code; no weighted long_hit component is affected.
- floor(n*frac) agrees with exact integer floors for every n < 8000 and all four fractions.
- LongScorer after the refactor: same cases against my own reference for its documented definition, both signs and default gates: match (same ic/long_ic caveat). tests/test_long_scorer.py 18 pass.
- PanelScorer: bit-identical to HEAD (HEAD's scoring.py + metrics.py loaded in a separate process): 1952 score records over 122 panels x kind x signed x penalty x gated, plus the raw bytes of rank_ic_turnover and _book_turnover_t.
- Look-ahead (240 perturbation trials, daily series captured by spying on _sharpe_ann): changing day t's label values or NaN pattern changes only day t's net and leaves turnover, to_*, long_tie, long_code, distinct exactly unchanged; changing day t's factor changes only days t and t+1; scoring the first T days reproduces the first T days of the full run exactly.
- Live-days rule: matches for every book (from the first day with a book; no-label days dropped; an all-NaN factor day is an empty book that pays liquidation and re-entry).
- Label exactly 0: counted as a loss under boundary z (strict >), both in the book and in the market base rate, so hit - base stays consistent; for auc it goes in the loser group. With VWAP-ratio labels exact zeros are negligible in production.
- All-up / all-down days: hit_top*, hit_ramp, hit_exp count the day as exactly 0 (not skipped), which shrinks them by the share of such days identically for every factor (half the days all-up: hit_top10_z 0.137 -> 0.067); auc / auc_long skip the day (0.0434 -> 0.0427, equal to the informative days alone). No cross-factor bias, and with about 5000 labelled names such days do not occur.
- Unbuyable names in the book: hold their weight, earn 0, pay turnover, and are excluded from hit denominators — as defined; conservative, not exploitable.
- Performance at (1359, 5220) float32, on a Mac that was heavily loaded by other jobs (load average 16-30), so treat absolute times as upper bounds: long_hit score() 4.0 s wall at 10 threads / 6.4 s CPU single-thread; LongScorer 3.8 s; PanelScorer rank_ic 1.2 s. So about the same cost as the first version and about 3x the old reward. Profile at quarter width: _prepare 41%, _hit_side 44%, _structure 10%. Peak RSS about 1.0 GB (0.5 GB scorer state + 0.3-0.5 GB transient measured; my count of live tensors in _hit_side gives up to about 16 float64 panels = 0.9 GB transient, which memory compression here may have hidden).
- Tests run without writing caches: test_long_hit_scorer.py + test_long_scorer.py 29 passed; test_chain_next, test_label_metrics, test_mining, test_rl_miners, test_tokens_env, test_pool, test_universe_mining 82 passed. The rest of the suite was not run.

issues.what: Orientation is chosen by top-10% GROSS excess, but the fit is made of net top-20% / rank-weighted books plus long-half hit rates and rank IC. When the two ends of a factor differ in turnover or shape, the chosen orientation can have a far lower fit than the other one. It can only under-reward (chosen fit <= max over orientations, which is what the first version takes); it never pays a bad factor more, and it is deterministic and symmetric under negation.
issues.evidence: Constructed case (orient_repro.py, D=1000, S=300, seed 3): f = where(fast in its top 10%, 10 + fast, -slow), both ends predictive. Gross top-10% excess +9.3 bp/day (+1) vs +4.6 (-1), so score() picks +1 with fit -0.0248 (to_top10 0.90, xs_top20 -7.4); orientation -1 has fit +0.0049 (to_top10 0.22). Gap 0.030 = one full fit unit; LongScorer picks -1. Frequency (orient.py, 450 synthetic persistent factors, D=1000, S=300, IC 0 to 0.02, one style factor in returns): lower-fit orientation chosen in 12.9% overall. Excluding the constructed two-speed family: 7.2% (monotone 5.6%, bottom-tail 3.3%, top-tail 6.7%, U-shape 13.3%), but the loss is small: gap > 0.003 in 1.9%, > 0.01 in 0.6%, max 0.013; with true IC >= 0.01 only about 2% are mis-oriented, and 2.8% of the top-20% by best-orientation fit. Two-speed family: 35.6% mis-oriented, gap > 0.01 in 20%, max 0.038 (sample p99 of fit is 0.030). Choosing by net top-10% instead does not help (14.4% overall) because 4 of 6 weight units are gross components. Caveat: synthetic returns, so fit magnitudes are not calibrated to production.
issues.fix: When both orientations pass the tie / code gates, run _hit_side for both and keep the higher fit, as LongScorer does (about +45% per score, since _hit_side is 44% of score()). Before deciding, measure it on the server without touching the runs: score the calibration library or the gp_hit_1 archive leaders with orientations=(1,) and (-1,) and count how many have fit(other) - fit(chosen) > 0.005.

issues.what: sh_top20 and sh_rankw are the portfolio's own Sharpe, so they carry the benchmark's Sharpe over each factor's own live window. Two consequences: (a) fit has a level offset of 0.03 x (0.5/0.43 + 0.5/0.2) / 6 = 0.0183 per 1.0 of market Sharpe, so fit = 0 is not 'no skill' and RL's MIN_SOLO=0 bar is shifted by that amount (laxer if the training-window benchmark Sharpe is positive, stricter if negative); (b) a factor with a longer warm-up starts its live window later and gets a different market Sharpe for free. GP ranking is unaffected by (a); (b) tilts ranking slightly toward long or nested windows if the first months of the sample were a bear market.
issues.evidence: semantics.py, D=1359, S=400, synthetic market with benchmark Sharpe 0.84: a factor that never changes (no skill, no turnover after day 0; xs_top20 -0.05, xs_rankw +0.05) scores fit +0.0158, half of the 0.03 level quoted as the library's 99th percentile. Same factor with its first 120 days set to NaN, in a market whose first 120 days were weak (benchmark Sharpe 0.836 over all days, 0.910 from day 120): fit 0.0304 -> 0.0326, of which about +0.0014 is the two sh_ components (sh_top20 0.916 -> 1.005, sh_rankw 0.830 -> 0.900). Mined expressions use day windows up to 60, nested up to about 120 days, so first-valid days differ by that much. I could not measure the real benchmark path locally.
issues.fix: Report sh_ relative to the benchmark over the same live days: _sharpe_ann(net[live])[0] - _sharpe_ann(self._ew_all[live])[0], then recalibrate the two sh_ scales. Until then, compute the Sharpe of scorer._ew_all on the server over all labelled days and from day 60 / 120; multiply by 0.0183 to get the offset of the MIN_SOLO bar and the size of the warm-up tilt. If the offset is material, set MIN_SOLO to that value for the next RL round instead of 0.

issues.what: A day on which one side is constant at a value that is not exactly representable returns about 0 (or 1e-17) instead of NaN, because the variance is rounding residue rather than exactly 0. The day is then counted as a zero-correlation day in ic / lic / long_ic and as a scored day for the min_scored_days gate. Pre-existing (identical at HEAD), not introduced by this change. No weighted long_hit component is affected: lric uses half-integer ranks, whose mean is exact. LongScorer's long_ic (weight 0.5) is exposed in principle, but a fully tied long half is rejected by the boundary-tie gate.
issues.evidence: _cs_corr_days_t(arange(7)[None], full((1,7), 0.0123)) returns 0.0, and with a constant factor 0.3 against random labels returns 1.46e-17; 0.01, 0.5, 1.0 correctly give NaN. In the fuzz, 67 of 700 cases (all containing a constant-label day) differ from the reference in ic / lic / long_ic, e.g. seed 42, shape (9, 55): ic 0.1125 vs 0.1266. No other key differs in any case.
issues.fix: Use a relative variance threshold, e.g. ok = (n >= MIN_PAIRS) & (va > 1e-20 * n * am*am + tiny) & (same for vb), or test row max == row min over the valid cells. Can wait; in production a whole-day constant label does not occur.

issues.what: The docstring says auc is P(a winner ranks above a loser) - 0.5 and equals half the difference of the two groups' mean u. The mean-u difference itself equals P - 0.5, so the code's auc (0.5 x difference) is half of P - 0.5. Scale only: auc is not in HIT_WEIGHTS and scales are calibrated from the same code, so no reward changes.
issues.evidence: semantics.py section 3: auc_z = 0.16943 while brute-force P(winner above loser) - 0.5 over all pairs = 0.33886, ratio exactly 2.0000. Two-name example: winner on top gives u 0.75 vs 0.25, difference 0.5 = AUC - 0.5, code returns 0.25.
issues.fix: Fix the docstring (auc = (P - 0.5) / 2), or drop the 0.5 factor and double the auc_z / auc_m scales.

issues.what: Two edge behaviours of the live-days rule that match the stated definition but are worth knowing. (1) Trading cost booked on a day with no label at all disappears with the dropped day. (2) The rankw book opens on a day with a single finite name (100% in it), while top5/10/20 and ramp need 2 names and hit rates need 5, so rankw can start one day earlier than the others. Neither matters in production: only the trailing horizon days lack labels, and single-name days do not survive the 0.8 coverage gate in any meaningful number.
issues.evidence: nolabel_cost.py, D=8, S=20, day 3 unlabelled: replacing the book on day 3 charges total turnover 1.0 over the live days (entry only); replacing it on day 4 charges 2.0. With day 0 holding one finite name, live days per book are top5/top10/top20/ramp = 6 and rankw = 7.
issues.fix: Optional: carry the cost of an unlabelled day into the next live day, and require n >= 2 for rankw. Can wait.

issues.what: Passing boundaries= that does not cover a weighted hit component is accepted at construction and then raises KeyError inside composite() on the first score(). Not reachable through make_scorer / the CLI, which never pass boundaries.
issues.evidence: LongHitScorer(y, weights={all components: 1}, scales=..., boundaries=('z',)).score(x) raises KeyError: 'hit_top5_m' (hit while writing nolabel_cost.py).
issues.fix: In __init__, raise ValueError if any weighted hit_ / auc key ends in a boundary not in self.boundaries, or always take the union of the two.

result.summary:
Scope of the verdict: rl_hit_1 only. gp_hit_1 should keep running; nothing I found changes its reward or would crash it.

RL (rl_hit_1): the new below-bar reward gives PPO a stationary safe harbour. A candidate below the bar is paid its own fitness (about -0.02) every time it is emitted, while re-emitting a pool member is paid -1. On a synthetic cube (150 names x 260 days, alphagen, 2000 episodes, bar 0, two seeds) the policy collapsed onto one junk expression and the pool stopped growing after the first quarter. Paying repeats of a below-bar key the -1 penalty (monkeypatched, same seed) restored exploration: 46 admissions instead of 9. This is synthetic evidence; I could not check production.

Before killing anything, read rl_hit_1_run.log (I did not touch the server):
- **Collapsed:** the `pool` number in the progress lines has stopped growing and batches fly by (everything is cached). Let it finish, because RL has no checkpoints and killing it loses the pool it has. Then patch and relaunch.
- **Still early or pool still growing slowly:** kill, patch, relaunch.

Checked and fine:
- **Tests:** the requested pytest command gives 88 passed.
- **CLI smokes on a synthetic store:** all exit 0 and write a run dir. Covered gp + long_hit (with rolling-block, ban-top-n, ban-rank-corr, archive-dedup), alphagen + long_hit + `--rl-min-solo 0` with inherited bans, alphaqcm / alphaforge / alphasage / warmstart with long_hit + bar 0, and the old paths (gp and alphagen with `--fitness rank_ic --turnover-penalty 0.14`, gp with `--fitness ic`).
- **Empty pool:** all five RL miners with an unreachable bar finish without a crash ("pool is empty; nothing to report", exit 1, nothing written). A 1-member pool runs the full report with all 8 combine methods.
- **Fresh-policy pass rate at bar 0 (synthetic):** of 600 episodes 142 completed; 78 were gate-rejected, 60 below the bar, 4 at or above it (2.8% of completed, 0.7% of episodes). The pool does not stay empty there.
- **Solo-score cache:** safe. There are no stochastic operators, a failed chunk gives a None panel (never a partial one), and there is one engine per rewarder (the universe wrapper included). About 4 KB per entry, so under 10 MB at budget 2000.
- **GP checkpoints:** long_hit writes the `score_xs_top20` … `score_distinct` columns; rank_ic and ic headers are unchanged. Every archive consumer in scripts/ reads by column name, and merge_archives' `score_ic` / `score_rank_ic` / `score_turnover` are still written.
- **Launch scripts under bash 3.2:** empty BAN_ARGS / UNI_ARGS / SOLO_ARGS, the `nb=` line (prints 0), keys with commas, parentheses and `|w3`, FITNESS validation, MIN_SOLO=off, `--exemplar-cache ""` passed once and accepted, and every flag parsed by the real parser. There is no `set -u`, so bash 5 behaves the same. I had no bash 5 to run.
- **chain_next.new_bans:** correct on the sample line.
- **Inherited bans:** a second GP run inheriting 9 keys banned 7 new ones with zero overlap, no archived tree contained an inherited key, and the cumulative count included the inherited ones. No "everything banned" state at this scale.
- **Degenerate panels:** 15 cases (all-NaN, inf, constant, one column, …) through long_hit / long / rank_ic `score` and `score_combined` raised nothing and never returned a NaN fit.

issues.what: The below-bar reward is a stationary safe harbour for PPO (affects rl_hit_1 only, not GP). A candidate under the bar is paid max(solo, 0.5 x penalty), in practice its solo of about -0.02 (the -0.5 floor never binds for long_hit; pure daily noise scores about -0.1), and it is paid that again on every repeat. Re-emitting a pool member is paid -1 (DuplicateFactorError). So the best repeatable reward is a junk expression just under the bar, and the policy converges onto it and stops exploring. This changes which expressions the RL is paid for.
issues.evidence: Synthetic cube (150 names x 260 days x 24 min, planted signal), run_mining with alphagen, long_hit, rl_min_solo=0, budget 2000, default PPO settings. Seed 0: pool reached 9 in the first quarter and never grew; in the last quarter 417 of 417 completed expressions were below the bar, 401 of them `day_mean(Open)` at reward -0.0172; 317 unique expressions in the whole run. Seed 1: last quarter 409 of 412 below the bar (`day_median(Vwap/Low/Close/Open)`), 0 added. Counterfactual, same seed 0, with repeats of an already-paid below-bar key paid the penalty (monkeypatched): 1467 unique expressions, 54 unique with solo >= 0 (vs 9), 46 admissions (vs 9), 18 of them in the last quarter. Not verified on production data; the mechanism does not depend on the data.
issues.fix: In BatchRewarder keep a set of below-bar keys already paid. First time: max(solo, 0.5 x penalty). Repeat: self.penalty, with reason "... (repeat)". Update tests/test_long_hit_scorer.py::test_rl_pool_refuses_candidates_below_the_solo_bar to match. Rewrites with identical ranks (e.g. add(x, x)) are still distinct keys; a rank-level seen-index like archive_dedup would close that too. Then relaunch RL. Check rl_hit_1_run.log first; RL has no checkpoints, so killing it loses its pool.

issues.what: Pre-existing, not from this change, but it is the next attractor once the issue above is fixed. `added=True` and the pool's fitness are paid whenever try_add does not raise, even when the member pruned for capacity is the candidate itself and the pool is unchanged. Once the pool is full, any gate-passing non-duplicate candidate is paid the unchanged pool fitness, repeatedly.
issues.evidence: Same synthetic setup with no bar (the rl_long_1 regime): 1430 of 1625 completed expressions were "added" into a 10-member pool. In the last quarter 403 of 406 were "added", all at exactly +0.3389 (pool unchanged), e.g. `day_max(Close)` 81 times with solo -0.019 and `day_max(Amt)` 73 times with solo -0.066. With the bar on, this path needs solo >= bar, so it is rarer but still open.
issues.fix: After try_add, check whether the candidate is actually a member (`expr in self.pool`). If it is not, treat it as not added and pay it like a below-bar candidate (solo once, penalty on repeats). Ship in the same patch as the fix above.

issues.what: Bar 0 is not break-even. Two fitness components are the absolute Sharpe of long-only books, so they carry the market's own Sharpe: the fitness of a static, zero-information, zero-turnover factor is about 0.0183 x (equal-weight market Sharpe over the training window). With a positive market Sharpe, no-information low-turnover characteristics clear MIN_SOLO=0; with a negative one, real factors must first overcome the offset. GP ranking is barely affected, since the offset is nearly common to all factors.
issues.evidence: make_scorer(target, "long_hit") on a synthetic 600 x 1000 target, static random factor. Market Sharpe +0.90 gives fit +0.0129; +0.13 gives +0.0004; -1.11 gives -0.0122. For comparison, a slow AR(0.98) no-information factor scores -0.004 / -0.012 / -0.027 and daily noise about -0.09 to -0.13. The production market Sharpe is not known to me.
issues.fix: At launch compute the offset (score a static random panel once, or 0.0183 x market Sharpe) and set MIN_SOLO = offset + margin. Alternatively apply the bar to fitness minus that offset. This is a next-launch tuning change; it does not need its own restart.

issues.what: No crash with an empty or 1-member pool, but an empty pool writes nothing: run_dir is None, there is no members.csv or meta.json, and the exit code is 1. RL has no checkpoints, so every solo score computed during the run is discarded, and a killed RL run leaves nothing either.
issues.evidence: run_mining with rl_min_solo=1e9 for alphagen, alphaqcm, alphaforge, alphasage and warmstart: all return pool=0, run_dir=None, "best reward -inf", last log line "pool is empty; nothing to report". CLI with --pool-capacity 1: full report, members.csv and combined.npy written, 8 combine methods fine.
issues.fix: Dump rew._solo_scores (expression, fit, components) to <run>/solo_scores.csv before the empty-pool return and at normal exit, ideally every N batches as well. Then an RL run with a strict bar is never a total loss.

issues.what: new_bans mis-parses an empty ban line. "封禁 0 个一层结构,累计生效 N 个: " followed by a newline makes the regex's `\s*` cross the line break and capture the next log line as a key. GP then dies at start-up in check_ban_key (loud). RL never validates --ban keys, so a malformed key is silently carried and bans nothing.
issues.evidence: new_bans("  封禁 0 个一层结构,累计生效 3 个: \n  按 rank 相关封禁:本块新增样本 0 个,累计 41 个\n") returns ['按 rank 相关封禁:本块新增样本 0 个,累计 41 个']. The sample line from the task parses correctly into 3 keys. A zero-ban line needs a block whose final population has no finite fitness: unlikely at population 64, but the small smoke run did produce a 1-key ban line.
issues.fix: Use `[::][ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$` and keep only keys starting with `O:`. Call gp.check_ban_key on the RL path too (pipeline.py, before building BatchRewarder).

issues.what: MIN_SOLO as a negative number in scientific notation is rejected by argparse, because `--rl-min-solo -1e-3` looks like an option. Plain negative decimals work.
issues.evidence: Stubbed dry run with the real parser: MIN_SOLO=-0.01 parses to rl_min_solo=-0.01; MIN_SOLO=-1e-3 fails with "argument --rl-min-solo: expected one argument", exit 2 (immediate and loud).
issues.fix: SOLO_ARGS=("--rl-min-solo=${MIN_SOLO:-0}")

issues.what: `--rl-min-solo` is silently ignored when no scorer is built (`--fitness ic` with turnover penalty 0), and for GP. The help text says the candidate "is paid that fitness", but the code pays max(solo, 0.5 x penalty). Neither affects the current runs.
issues.evidence: Code path: pipeline.py:399 builds a scorer only if kind != "ic" or penalty > 0; env.py:245 requires `self.scorer is not None`.
issues.fix: Raise in cmd_mine when --rl-min-solo is given with --fitness ic and no turnover penalty, or with --miner gp. Correct the help text.

issues.what: Unverified risk. With BAN_FROM, RL loads the rank-ban exemplars in 150-tree engine calls under a 0.3 GPU cap, and the tolerant engine drops trees silently on CUDA OOM. The log line cannot tell OOM drops from the 0.99 exemplar dedup.
issues.evidence: Code reading only. The comment at gp.py:478 records 462 exemplars in one call using 31.9 of 32.6 GB; scaled linearly, 150 trees is about 10 GB against a cap of about 9.8 GB. Locally on CPU, 23 of 23 loaded.
issues.fix: Compare "rank-ban exemplars: N 个" in rl_hit_1_run.log with the `exemplars` count on gp_hit_1's first generation line. Same archive, keys and view, so they should be equal. If RL's is smaller, lower the batch for RL (e.g. 50) and log how many panels came back None.

issues.what: BAN_FROM is not transitive. A run's log only prints the bans it made itself, not the ones it inherited, so round 3 must list every earlier run (BAN_FROM="gp_long_1 gp_hit_1"). Listing only the latest silently drops the older bans and their archive. Separately, the gp_long.sh header still says it inherits nothing.
issues.evidence: Smoke run gp_d inherited 9 keys from gp_a; its own log's ban lines list only its 7 new keys. new_bans on that log returns 7. Keys duplicated across several runs are harmless (frozenset).
issues.fix: Document it in the script header, or have the script echo the inherited keys in the same "封禁" format so one log carries the full chain.

result.summary:
No exploit found that lets a zero-skill candidate beat a good honest factor, so neither job needs to be killed. One real reward bug should be fixed before the next launch, and the gp_hit_1 archive should be re-scored with that fix before anyone reads its leaderboard.

All numbers are from synthetic (panel, label) pairs scored with LongHitScorer at default weights (750x1200, 1000x1200, 1359x800, 300x5000; market vol 1.2%, per-name vol 1-5%, junk decile -10bp/day, 1% NaN labels). Reference points: honest slow factor (long-half rank IC ~0.015, top-20% turnover 11%/day) fit +0.027 to +0.046; static noise = offset +/- 0.003; iid noise -0.10.

Ranked by damage:
1. **Late start (real bug).** sh_top20 / sh_rankw are absolute Sharpes measured from the candidate's first holding day. A candidate that is NaN through an opening bear leg gets the later market's Sharpe for free: +0.005 to +0.013 fit on a 2018-shaped 1359-day sample. The GP and RL vocabularies both contain operators that do this (cross_delay / cross_delta / cross_hurst with window 241).
2. **Benchmark Sharpe offset.** Every candidate carries 0.0183 x benchmark Sharpe, so MIN_SOLO=0 is not a skill bar.
3. **Low-vol tilt.** A zero-alpha low-vol sort earns 25-40% of an honest factor's margin over noise.
4. **xs_* pathology.** Negative Sharpe improves with tracking error and is unbounded below.
5. **Short-side information** is paid at about half the honest rate.
6-9. Static drift, orientation bias, dropped days and ties are small or not exploitable.

Why not restart: the late-start bonus is additive and identical for every carrier, carriers are the same factor with a shorter history, and offline re-scoring repairs the ranking. Restart gp_hit_1 only if its newest checkpoint already shows more than about 30% of the top 50 carrying a 241-window cross_delay / cross_delta / cross_hurst, or the block-end bans are being spent on those structures.

Not verifiable locally: the production benchmark Sharpe, the real 2018 path, and whether the store supplies 60 warm-up rows (late start 181 days) or none (241 days, mostly blocked by the 0.8 coverage gate).

A background null-distribution run hit its time limit and was re-run with smaller samples. Results from an earlier interrupted pass in the same scratch folder (n=120 per noise type) agree. Scripts and outputs: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-230P-hw2/208bbacf-e83a-42e0-b6f4-3ead427e5e95/scratchpad/hit/

issues.what: Late start. `live` begins at the candidate's first holding day and sh_top20 / sh_rankw are the absolute Sharpe of net[live]. A candidate that is NaN during an opening bear leg is credited with the later market's Sharpe, with no skill. Recipe: any expression containing cross_delay, cross_delta or cross_hurst with window 241, e.g. sub(X, sub(L, L)) with L = cross_delay(day_mean(Ret), 241), which equals X from day 241 on. Components paying: sh_rankw (about two thirds) and sh_top20. The first version (LongScorer) is unaffected. Likelihood: high. Not a restart because the bonus is additive and the same for every carrier, and the archive can be re-scored offline; restart GP only if the newest checkpoint's top 50 is already more than about 30% carriers.
issues.evidence: Real engine on a synthetic store: cross_delay(X, 241), cross_delta and cross_hurst give first valid day 240-241; ts_delay / ts_delta / ts_pearson / ts_spearman / ts_hurst give 49-50; every other windowed operator uses partial windows (day 0-2). All three cross operators with 241 are in the GP generator and the RL vocabulary; 0.95% of 6000 random GP trees (depth 3-5) contain one, so roughly 12 per 1280 evaluations before window mutation. End to end with a zero-information factor X = ts_mean(day_std(Ret), 20): fit -0.0261, the late-started twin -0.0129. Production-shaped test (1359 days, first 200 lose 33%, then ~12%/yr): first valid day 181 adds +0.0046 (seed 0) and +0.0090 (seed 1) on average; day 241 adds up to +0.0134. Static noise goes 0.0026 -> 0.0106 and 0.0071 -> 0.0160, above a clean honest factor at 0.0145. An honest factor with twice the noise, late-started (0.0307), ties the clean best (0.0312). Late-starting every second candidate drops the rank correlation with the clean ordering to 0.85-0.87. Harsher 1000-day test (-30% in first 150 days): +0.010 to +0.015; static noise 0.0138 -> 0.0289 against honest 0.0319.
issues.fix: In _hit_side: out[f"sh_{name}"] = _sharpe_ann(net[live])[0] - _sharpe_ann(self._ew_all[live])[0]. Checked: the bonus falls from +0.008..+0.010 to -0.0015..+0.0003 in one seed and from +0.0044..+0.0067 to +0.002..+0.0044 in the other (the remainder is genuine regime luck; only a common burn-in of ~241 days for all candidates removes it). Re-score the gp_hit_1 archive with this before ranking it.

issues.what: sh_top20 and sh_rankw contain the benchmark's own Sharpe, so every candidate carries a constant 0.03 x (0.5/0.43 + 0.5/0.20) / 6 = 0.0183 x benchmark Sharpe. GP ordering is unaffected, but MIN_SOLO=0 stops being a skill bar: its meaning depends on the sign of the in-sample market Sharpe. Separately, fit >= 0 does not mean 'profitable after cost', because two thirds of the weight is cost-free. Noise in sh_rankw does not dominate the fit; what moves it is rankw turnover cost, real excess, and the sample window. Likelihood: certain. Affects only which RL candidates are offered to the pool.
issues.evidence: Static noise passes fit > 0 in 95% of 120 draws when benchmark Sharpe is +0.27 (mean fit +0.0058, sd 0.0033, max +0.0159), and in 42% of 40 draws when it is -0.13 (mean -0.0007, sd 0.0030). AR(0.999) noise: 78% vs 12%. AR(0.99): 0%. First version: 75-82% and 45-50%. Cross-candidate sd for static noise: sh_top20 0.07 (0.16 scale, +/-0.4e-3 fit), sh_rankw 0.016-0.02 (0.08-0.10 scale, +/-0.2e-3). Low-beta tilt under a flat security market line: sh_top20 +0.18, sh_rankw +0.05, i.e. +0.0016 fit; NaN on the highest-vol 19%: +0.0009 to +0.0018; zero under CAPM. Fast accurate factor (long-half rank IC 0.018-0.020, top-20% turnover 70%/day, top-20% net excess -22% to -30%/yr): fit +0.001 to +0.017, so it passes the bar. Same alpha with autocorrelation 0.8 (net excess -5%/yr): +0.014 to +0.017.
issues.fix: The benchmark-relative sh_ change from the first issue removes the offset. Then set MIN_SOLO to the null mean plus 3 sd (about 0.010-0.015 measured on real labels with ~20 random static rankings), or bar on xs_top20 >= 0 if the intent is 'not a money-loser standalone'. Leave rl_hit_1 running; relaunch with a higher MIN_SOLO only if its pool fills with near-static or loss-making members.

issues.what: A pure low-vol or low-beta sort with zero mean alpha is paid. The 'return > 0' boundary and the rank-based lric reward a higher median, not a higher mean: low-vol names win more often under positive market drift and under right-skewed returns. The reward is not mostly a vol tilt (honest still wins 2-3x), but the tilt collects 25-40% of an honest factor's margin over noise, and bolting a low-beta tilt onto any factor adds fit. The first version pays about half as much. Likelihood: certain (day_std(Ret) is a primitive, and the first-version runs already converged on low-activity names).
issues.evidence: Static low-vol sort forced to the low-vol side, mean of 6 world seeds. Gaussian, equal means, beta 1: fit 0.0125 vs static noise 0.0060 vs honest 0.0319 (first version 0.0046). Lognormal skew, equal arithmetic means: 0.0167 vs 0.0060 vs 0.0320; contributions x1e-3: hit_exp_z +3.3, lric +3.0, auc_long_z +2.3, sh_top20 +2.3, sh_rankw +4.6 (noise gets 1.9 and 4.3 from the offset), xs ~0. Flat security market line plus skew: 0.0094 vs -0.0017 vs 0.0311. CAPM: -0.0004, no payment. Junk decile = highest-vol decile (real alpha): 0.0155 vs 0.0009 vs 0.0309. With free orientation the low-vol side is chosen only 50-67% of the time in the zero-alpha worlds (fit 0.005-0.013). Adding a static low-beta tilt to a fast honest factor: 0.0009 -> 0.0126 and 0.0155 -> 0.0239 (lric +0.005, auc_long_z +0.0018); the opposite tilt: -0.0174 and +0.0075.
issues.fix: Nothing for the running jobs. When ranking the archive, report each top factor's rank correlation with a plain trailing-vol sort and discount near-duplicates. For the next version, compute the win boundary and lric within vol buckets (or on vol-neutralised labels).

issues.what: xs_top20 and xs_rankw are Sharpes of net excess: unbounded below, and for a net-negative candidate they improve when tracking error is added. Among cost-dominated candidates (most of the search early on, and every RL candidate below the bar) the ordering is partly 'more tracking error is better'. The same loss rate scores very differently depending on how noisy the factor's payoff is, and the penalty grows with universe size. On the upside nothing swamps: hit and lric contributions are bounded near +15 to +20e-3. sh_* still carries a linear cost term, so cost is not lost entirely. Likelihood: certain, but it affects ordering only below zero.
issues.evidence: iid noise at 15bp: xs_top20 -22.7 (-12 scales, -30e-3 fit), xs_rankw -32 (-16 scales, -40e-3), sh_top20 -3.1 (-18e-3), sh_rankw -1.4 (-17e-3), fit -0.105. At 5000 names: xs_top20 -48, xs_rankw -57 to -63 (-71 to -78e-3), fit -0.155 to -0.173. Same iid noise with NaN on the highest-vol 19% of names (same turnover, same annual loss): xs_rankw -31 -> -11, fit -0.113 -> -0.086 and -0.111 -> -0.082. With all-NaN on a random 19% of days: -0.117 -> -0.074 and -0.102 -> -0.051. Fast honest factor losing ~23%/yr in the top-20% book: fit -0.010 when its payoff is steady (xs -10.4 / -15.3) and +0.002 to +0.017 when volatile (xs -2.2 / -2.5).
issues.fix: Floor the xs_* term at about -3 scales, or use xa_top20 / xa_rankw (scales already in HIT_SCALES) when the mean is negative. Wait for the next launch.

issues.what: Short-side information is paid. rankw minus the equal-weight benchmark is a rank-weighted long-short book, and hit_exp_z compares the top with a market-wide base rate that includes the junk. A factor that only identifies losers, with no information inside the long half, earns about half of an honest factor's margin; the first version pays 20-35%. auc_long_z and lric behave correctly (about 0). This is the only coverage game that pays: dropping random or high-vol names does not. Likelihood: high, since most minute-bar anomalies are short-side.
issues.evidence: Static noise with the junk decile pushed to the bottom: fit -0.0006 vs -0.0122 for plain noise (+0.0116) and 0.0158 vs 0.0062 (+0.0096); first version +0.005 and +0.003. Same result when the junk decile is NaN instead (+0.010, +0.009): xs_rankw +2.4 to +2.8 (+3.0 to +3.5e-3), sh_rankw +1.7 to +2.0e-3, hit_exp_z +0.0026 to +0.0029, xs_top20 +0.8 to +1.5e-3. Alpha only below the median (top half static noise): margin over noise +0.015 / +0.020 / +0.008 against honest +0.029 / +0.038 / +0.020 (40-52%); hit_exp_z +0.0074 to +0.0107, auc_long_z ~0, lric ~0.001. Alpha only above the median scores the same as the full honest factor. Honest factor with NaN on a random 19% of names: -0.000 to -0.004; on the highest-vol 19%: +0.002.
issues.fix: Swap rankw for ramp in HIT_WEIGHTS (xs_ramp / sh_ramp are already computed and scaled; calibration shows ramp at least as predictive), and take hit_exp_z's base rate from the long half rather than the whole market. Wait for the next launch.

issues.what: Static rankings have zero turnover, so any constant ranking correlated with persistent per-name drift is paid through xs_rankw and xs_top20. This is in-sample style fitting, but it is no worse than in the first version, and it needs a characteristic that is genuinely correlated with the drift. Likelihood: medium (price level, size and liquidity are near-static).
issues.evidence: Per-name drift sd 2bp/day, two world seeds. Static sort on the true drift: fit 0.0138 / 0.0334 (first version 0.0190 / 0.0281), honest 0.0101 / 0.0429; xs_rankw 5.4-5.9 (+7e-3), xs_top20 3.0-3.7. Characteristic correlated 0.5 with drift: 0.0068 / 0.0172 (first version 0.0181 / 0.0044). Correlated 0.25: -0.0081 / 0.0117. Static noise: -0.0136 / +0.0135 (the offset). Causal trailing-250-day mean return: -0.016 / +0.008, i.e. nothing. Sorting on the in-sample realised mean (look-ahead, unreachable): 0.070 / 0.088.
issues.fix: None needed now. Out-of-sample checking of the archive already covers it.

issues.what: Orientation is chosen by the top-10% gross excess and only that side is scored. This gives pure noise a small positive bias, far below an honest fit. The noise floor comes from lric, xs_top20 and auc_long_z, not from the sh_ terms.
issues.evidence: Static noise, 40 draws, benchmark Sharpe -0.13: chosen orientation mean -0.0007, forced +1 mean -0.0025, so the bias is +0.0018 (0.55 sd); sd 0.0030, max +0.0060. Per-component noise in fit units: lric +/-1.0e-3, xs_top20 +/-0.7e-3, auc_long_z +/-0.6e-3, xs_rankw +/-0.5e-3, hit_exp_z +/-0.45e-3, sh_top20 +/-0.4e-3, sh_rankw +/-0.2e-3. AR(0.999) noise -0.0040 +/- 0.0028; AR(0.99) -0.0109; AR(0.9) -0.0317; iid -0.105. Earlier pass with 120 draws: static max sits 0.011 above the offset. Honest: 0.0427 +/- 0.0020, weaker honest 0.0267 +/- 0.0039.
issues.fix: None needed.

issues.what: Dropped days are not exploitable apart from the leading-NaN case in the first issue. Scattered all-NaN days are punished (liquidation both ways plus sitting in cash), days with fewer than 5 names are punished harder, and hit averages do not move. The only thing that would pay is real market timing, which the sh_ terms reward at a very high rate.
issues.evidence: All-NaN on a random 19% of days: honest 0.0079 -> -0.0188 and 0.0436 -> 0.0190; static noise -0.0121 -> -0.0417 and 0.0074 -> -0.0142; hit_exp_z changes by at most 0.0004. Causal rule 'NaN the day after a bad market day': honest -0.0022 / 0.0261, i.e. worse. Three names on a random 19% of days: honest -0.0152 / 0.0055. Foresight (NaN on the 19% worst market days): static noise +0.088 / +0.123, with sh_rankw 4.2-5.9 (+53 to +74e-3).
issues.fix: None beyond the benchmark-relative sh_ change, which also removes the timing payment.

issues.what: u is the sorted position, so inside a tie block it is the stock's column number, and only the top-10% book boundary is gated for ties and code order. A factor with the bottom half tied, or with a tie block straddling the top-20% boundary, passes the gates and gets a code-ordered rankw / top-20% book in that block. The effect is small even in a worst case.
issues.evidence: Columns re-ordered so that column number equals the low-vol rank. Bottom half tied: fit -0.0009 -> -0.0004 and 0.0099 -> 0.0090. Ranks 45-85% collapsed with the top 15% distinct: -0.0007 and 0.0074. Both pass the gates; pure column number is still rejected (code = 1.0).
issues.fix: Use average ranks for u, or extend the tie check to the top-20% boundary. Can wait.
